title: kernel mosaic bench: int8 / awq / fp8 interaction notes
content:
Purpose and quick summary:
This doc is a lightweight investigative diary capturing an unusual interaction observed when mixing multiple quant kernels across workloads. The shorthand I started using is 'kernel mosaic' — patches of execution where different kernel implementations dominate contiguous token windows and create non-linear latency/quality artifacts. The goal: record experiment matrix, surprising failure modes, and quick mitigations to try in the next sprint.

Background / motivation:
- We've been comparing INT8 (gptq), AWQ-style per-channel schemes, and experimental FP8 paths across the usual microbench harnesses. Previous runs treated kernel variants independently. During a long-context replay test, we saw throughput dips and occasional perplexing quality regressions not present when the same kernel was used exclusively.
- Hypothesis: switching between kernels at layer boundaries or at dispatcher multiplex points creates micro-cache/tiling churn + numerical edge cases that increase compute time and occasionally perturb softmax activations in a measurable way.

Environment:
- Model: rwg-13b-ref (decoder-only, 8k context), tokenizer standard BPE used in production harness
- Hardware: A100-80GB, CUDA 12.1, cuBLAS 12.1, custom kernel set v2.7.1 (includes int8-gptq, awq-blockwise, fp8-emul)
- Orchestration: local dedicated node, single process multi-stream harness, simulated traffic mix (60% short chat, 40% long-context generation)
- Tooling: microbench harness v0.9.9, perf counters, nvprof / nsight sampling, and our in-house KV stress shim that forces frequent KV prefetch/evict events.

Experiment matrix (high level):
- Axis 1: quant format / kernel family: INT8-GPTQ (baseline kernel K_gptq_v5), AWQ-block (K_awq_v2), FP8-emulated (K_fp8_v1)
- Axis 2: routing patterns: homogeneous (single kernel per run), alternating-layer (switch kernel every N layers where N=1,2,4), runtime-mosaic (dispatcher switches kernel per-request based on size/latency budget)
- Axis 3: sequence mix: short-only (<=64 tokens), long-only (>=2048 tokens), mixed-live (realistic 60/40 mix)

Key observations (raw):
1) Homogeneous runs behave as expected: INT8 fastest median latency, AWQ slightly slower but similar throughput efficiency, FP8 slower but more stable numeric fidelity on certain prompts. No anomalies.
2) Alternating-layer runs show a 7-15% increase in 95th percentile latency compared to homogenous baseline; variance increases with N=1 (i.e., switch every layer).
3) Runtime-mosaic policy produces spikes: while median latency close to baseline, tail latency and jitter are substantially worse. Spikes correlate with bursts of long-context requests that concurrently trigger kernel switch logic in the dispatcher.
4) In ~3% of mixed-live samples under runtime-mosaic, we saw token-level divergence (measured by logit-rank change > 5) compared to the homogenous-int8 baseline. These divergences cluster on sequences with long repetitive phrases that amplify tiny numerical differences.

Profiling notes (nvprof / counters):
- When kernel switches occur, we see short-lived increases in global memory traffic and L2 cache miss rate. Hypothesis: different kernels use different tiling and packing; switching invalidates prefetch patterns and forces re-packing of activation tiles into alternate layouts.
- Kernel K_awq_v2 uses a 64x32 tiling optimized for channel-major blocking; K_gptq_v5 prefers 128x16. The copy/packing kernels are small but become hot during churn.
- FP8 path triggers additional cast/expand steps and surprisingly increases register pressure in fused attention kernel variants, leading to more kernel launches (smaller fragments) and higher per-token overhead.

Quality diagnostics:
- Divergence cases are subtle: early-token softmax shapes changed by <1e-3 but for autoregressive sampling they cause different token choices later. Deterministic greedy decoding magnifies the effect across the remainder of the sequence.
- Running same mixed sequence deterministically (fixed seed, top-k=1) shows divergences only when kernel switches are enabled. Re-running with fully homogeneous FP8 or INT8 removes divergence.

Controlled microtest added:
- Introduced 'no-pack' toggle to skip repacking when switching kernels. This reduced latency spike magnitude by ~40% but increased steady-state memory bandwidth by ~10% — tradeoff.
- Added 'delayed-switch' (apply kernel switch only at layer boundaries where sequence position % 8 == 0). This lowered jitter and reduced divergence frequency to ~0.5%.

Quick numbers (median of 10 runs where applicable):
- Homogeneous INT8: p50=48ms, p95=72ms, throughput=210 req/s
- Alternating-layer (N=1): p50=52ms, p95=84ms, throughput=185 req/s
- Runtime-mosaic policy: p50=50ms, p95=110ms, throughput=195 req/s, divergence rate=3.0%
- Runtime-mosaic + delayed-switch: p50=51ms, p95=78ms, throughput=188 req/s, divergence rate=0.5%
- Homogeneous FP8-emul: p50=62ms, p95=90ms, throughput=165 req/s

Preliminary root-cause hypotheses and supporting evidence:
- Packing/layout impedance: switching causes the small packing kernels to dominate for short windows; evidence: spike in pack kernel occupancy in nvprof at time of spike.
- Register pressure fragmentation: FP8 path fosters smaller kernel launch sizes; evidence: increased kernel launch count and lower achieved SM occupancy per launch.
- Numerical sensitivity at boundary: when a layer output is repacked with slightly different alignment/scaling ordering, quantized rounding can cause a small bias that grows autoregressively. Evidence: rerun with higher precision accumulation (float32) at packing boundary reduces divergences.

Immediate mitigations to add to codebase (short tasks):
- Option A (fast): implement delayed-switch policy in dispatcher (config flag), default to layer-aligned switching or N>=2. Ticket GH-3472.
- Option B (packing): add a shared canonical pack buffer per-threadblock so pack layout remains consistent across kernels where possible. Spike: medium effort. Ticket GH-3499.
- Option C (numeric): force higher-precision accumulation for pack/unpack fringes in mixed-kernel scenarios. Quick patchable in 1-2 days. Ticket GH-3516.
- Option D (telemetry): add a per-request 'kernel-switch count' field to tracing and expose a histogram in console to correlate with tail latency and quality alerts. Ticket GH-3520.

Longer-term work / research directions:
- Formalize a 'mosaic' stress harness that intentionally mixes kernels to characterize boundary behavior across models and sequence distributions. Use it as a gate for new kernel rollouts.
- Explore a packing ABI so kernels share a canonical packed-activation layout, eliminating repack churn.
- Evaluate whether mixed-precision accumulation (selective higher precision) at layer boundaries recovers fidelity without major perf penalty.

Open questions / TODOs:
- How often does mosaic-induced divergence show up in user traffic? Need sampling of production traces with long repetitive tails. (CS / SRE request)
- Could we detect potentially unstable sequences online by a cheap heuristic (repetition score + recent kernel-switch history) and steer them to homogenous kernels?
- If delayed-switch is default, quantify cost across all models and request mixes — run full-matrix audit.

Immediate next steps (next 2 weeks):
1) Land delayed-switch feature behind flag + tiny sampling in staging traffic (Ari).
2) Add kernel-switch telemetry to request trace payloads (Ben).
3) Start canonical pack buffer spike (Rina) and measurement microbench to validate savings.
4) Collect production trace samples and run mosaic stress harness offline against top 20 frequent prompts (Sofia).

Appendix: quick commands used for microbench harness
- run harness: tools/microbench/run_local.sh --model rwg-13b-ref --kernels K_gptq_v5,K_awq_v2,K_fp8_v1 --mode runtime-mosaic --concurrency 32 --trace out/trace.mosaic
- nvprof sample: nvprof --analysis-metrics compute_occupancy,dram_read_throughput,l2_read_transactions -f --log-file nv_out.txt ./microbench ...
- divergence detector: tools/compare_logits.py --baseline out/homog_int8/logits.npy --probe out/mosaic/logits.npy --threshold 5

Notes to self: keep this document rough. Capture results and tickets, then convert a polished runbook if delayed-switch proves low-risk. If we end up adopting a canonical packing ABI, that will be a bigger project requiring API alignment with Private deployment package.

End.
